meta.title: Achieving SCD's Claimed TTFT-Quality Trade-offs via Method Improvements and Similarity Optimization

survey.literature_scope: Focused survey of Semantic Cache Distillation and closely related cross-model cache/state transfer methods, restricted to work relevant to prefix reuse, state/KV translation, selective patching, and TTFT-quality trade-offs.
key_references: Semantic Cache Distillation: Efficient State Transfer via Reuse and Selective Patching (local file: ICML2026_MaQianli.pdf)
SCD three-route validation checklist (local file: SCD_three_route_validation_checklist.md)
survey.synthesis_summary: The local paper claims that Semantic Cache Distillation can transfer prefix state across models with favorable TTFT-quality trade-offs. Experiments on the runnable Qwen3-1.7B near-pair now show that the clean original method and all three follow-up routes fail to achieve the claimed operating point. Under the stricter user-required no-fallback definition, Route A, Route B, and Route C all collapse to 0.0 F1 despite lower TTFT than their same-run full-consumer baselines. The remaining live question is therefore whether more compatible higher-similarity pairs or a materially different patch/recompute design can recover the claim at all.
open_gaps: Strict no-fallback reruns on the runnable Qwen3-1.7B near-pair now show that Route A, Route B, and Route C all fail catastrophically: every transfer route falls to 0.0 F1 once fallback overlay is removed.
Qwen3.5-4B pairs are blocked by hybrid cache architecture incompatibility with current SCD implementation.
Need to identify: (1) whether any materially different transfer formulation can recover usable quality without fallback, and (2) what level of model similarity is required.
Alternative model families with standard KV cache and high similarity may be needed if Qwen pairs remain blocked.

ideation.research_goal: Achieve the SCD paper's claimed TTFT-quality trade-offs through any effective combination of method improvements and model-pair similarity optimization. The goal is pragmatic success rather than strict reproduction: if a method variant works, use it; if current pairs are insufficient, find better ones.
ideation.problem_framing: Initial evidence now shows the clean original SCD method and all three follow-up routes fail on the runnable Qwen3-1.7B near-pair under the strict no-fallback definition, while Qwen3.5 pairs remain blocked by hybrid cache architecture incompatibility. Route A, Route B, and Route C all collapse to 0.0 F1 once fallback overlay is removed, so incremental tuning of the current Route A/B/C implementations on this pair is no longer justified. The project should therefore prioritize either alternative high-similarity pairs with standard KV cache semantics or a materially different patch/recompute design.
ideation.evidence_plan: Path 1 is now effectively closed for the current near-pair under the strict no-fallback definition: the clean original method, Route A, Route B, and Route C have all been measured, and every transfer route misses usable task quality. Any further method work on this pair should require a materially different patch/recompute formulation rather than another small configuration sweep. Path 2 is now primary: identify and acquire higher-similarity model pairs from families with standard KV cache architecture, then re-run the strongest available transfer baselines there.
success_criteria: At least one method variant (original, Route A/B/C, or hybrid) achieves the paper's claimed TTFT-quality trade-off on at least one model pair.
If no current pair supports the claim, identify and test at least two alternative high-similarity pairs from different model families.
Document the minimal conditions (method + similarity level) required to achieve the claimed effect.

experiment.hypothesis_or_validation_goal: The current evidence suggests that the SCD paper's claimed TTFT-quality trade-offs are not recovered by the clean original method or by Route A/B/C on the runnable Qwen3-1.7B near-pair. Strict no-fallback reruns now strengthen this conclusion: Route A, Route B, and Route C all fall to 0.0 F1 once fallback overlay is removed. The remaining live hypothesis is that the claimed operating point, if real, requires either more compatible higher-similarity pairs with standard KV cache semantics or a materially different patch/recompute design beyond the current Route A/B/C implementations.
experiment.dataset_or_data_source: Use the SCD paper's data/tasks, prefix construction, and evaluation settings as the primary data source. Use smaller calibration subsets for debugging, pair screening, and layerwise similarity estimation before full benchmark runs.
experiment.method_or_protocol: Revised protocol with two active paths and locked default transfer methods. Within this project, the term `SCD method` now refers only to the locked strict family: baseline, repaired reuse-only, current strict patch-only, and, when separately validated under the same contract, current strict hybrid. Path 1 (method exploration) now centers on strict no-fallback comparisons among baseline, repaired reuse-only, current strict patch-only, and the current strict hybrid on runnable pairs. The reuse route is locked to the repaired clean layerwise path only: group_size=1, batched encode/decode fast path, actual transfer timing, pure rebuild accounting, no fallback, and no recompute unless explicitly requested. The patch route is locked to the current strict patch-only branch only: dedicated patch_only runtime, no reuse scaffold, no fallback, no recompute, fit family `xnorm_nativekv_shared_residual_mlp_v1`, hidden transport `xnorm_a -> xb_hat`, consumer-native `Wk/Wv`, and only the consumer's own required post-projection operators (`K-only k_norm` when the architecture has it, plus native rotary handling). Patch-only TTFT must be charged strictly as `encode + transfer + wall-clock patch_infer + decode_first`; on Mistral-family runs where shared-process evaluation perturbs patch projection time, patch-only must be benchmarked in an isolated fresh process and merged afterward. The hybrid route is now also locked: patch-only anchor plus greedy blockwise reuse search, no fallback, no recompute, and immediate stop once replay quality-pass becomes empty; if a pair has no validated strict hybrid artifact, hybrid must be omitted rather than replaced by fallback-based history. Older grouped/shared-z reuse checkpoints, `reuse_fallback`, `reuse_patch`, `reuse_patch_recompute`, fallback-dependent comparisons, scaffold-mixed paths, and older patch fit families are retained only as failure analysis and must not be labeled as `SCD method` baselines. For `Mistral-7B -> MistralLite`, the canonical reverse-pair route source now points to `/Users/weimingming/dr-claw/scd-new/Experiment/analysis/mistral7_to_mistrallite_final_route_lock_20260409.md`, where the accepted pair-specific `SCD method` evidence currently includes only baseline, repaired reuse-only, and current strict patch-only; the later fallback-based Q2 reverse chain is archived-only. Path 2 (pair exploration) remains active: identify alternative higher-similarity pairs with standard KV cache semantics, including same-model precision variants and nearby fine-tunes such as Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 and Qwen3-1.7B-gray. For any new pair, the default serving comparison table must report only baseline, repaired reuse-only, current strict patch-only, and, when validated under the strict contract, current strict hybrid.
experiment.scd_method_lock_summary: The project now uses a single claim-facing meaning for `SCD method`: the locked strict transfer-method family consisting of baseline, repaired reuse-only, current strict patch-only, and, when separately validated under the same contract, current strict hybrid. Historical fallback/recompute/scaffold-mixed routes are archived-only and cannot be cited as SCD methods. For `Mistral-7B -> MistralLite`, the accepted pair-specific SCD-method artifact is `/Users/weimingming/dr-claw/scd-new/Experiment/analysis/mistral7_to_mistrallite_final_route_lock_20260409.md`, which currently validates only baseline/reuse-only/patch-only.
experiment.evaluation_plan: Run the original SCD baseline and, if needed, the three improved routes on matched calibration/validation/test prefixes with identical tokenizer, attention mask, and cache semantics. Emit prompt-level, run-level, and claim-level structured outputs so every claim can be traced from raw prompt rows to pair-level decisions. Judge the paper claim primarily through normalized local-vs-native ratios rather than raw cross-hardware milliseconds: TTFT ratio, task-quality retention, PPL ratio when available, KL ceilings when the paper's oracle-referenced KL baseline is zero, and payload ratio against the raw-KV transfer baseline. Primary outcomes are the component-wise claim gaps and the aggregate claim gap between measured TTFT-quality trade-offs and the SCD paper's reported target for the original method on similar pairs. Secondary outcomes are whether route A/B/C close or eliminate that gap, along with reconstruction error, layerwise transfer fidelity, gain-per-byte, gain-per-millisecond, and paired-bootstrap confidence intervals on all main deltas.
experiment.claim_target_summary: The claim target is now defined as a paper-normalized TTFT-quality operating point evaluated on preregistered close Qwen3.5 pairs. The claim table has been backfilled with two paper anchors: Table 1 Qwen Pair (32B) as the primary family-aligned target and Table 2 MistralLite→Mistral-7B at 200 Gbps as the detailed efficiency target. The original SCD baseline is judged by strict-pass, soft-pass, or fail criteria against TTFT ratio, task-quality retention, KL ceiling and PPL ratio when active, and payload ratio versus raw-KV transfer when claimed. If the original baseline fails, route A/B/C are judged on the same pairs by either full rescue or at least 50% aggregate claim-gap reduction.
experiment.baseline_protocol_summary: The baseline protocol now fixes candidate-pair admission rules, a close/medium/far screening workflow, original-SCD runtime semantics without suffix recomputation, patch-layer selection via the paper's restore-one plus greedy policy, paper-aligned task and metric requirements, and a compute schedule that uses 4090D for screening and A800 only for short-burst final runs.
experiment.evaluation_contract_summary: The evaluation contract now requires prompt-level, run-level, and claim-level outputs with fixed schemas for TTFT, latency breakdown, task quality, KL, TV, PPL, payload, and claim-gap metrics. Qwen3.5 headline judgments default to the Table 1 Qwen Pair anchor, while the Table 2 MistralLite→Mistral-7B anchor is mandatory for detailed efficiency analysis. Baseline and route comparisons must use matched operating points and report paired-bootstrap confidence intervals plus route rescue labels. For the active Qwen3-1.7B route reruns, matched first-token timing is now the default measurement convention so full_consumer and transfer paths share the same cache-based first-decode boundary.
experiment.reviewer_q2_mistral7_to_mistrallite_fres: A fully fresh Reviewer Q2 rerun for `Mistral-7B -> MistralLite` was completed on April 7, 2026 on `ser` under run root `/disk_n/c101-3-1/projects/scd-repro-codex-mistral-instruct-20260323/runs/scd-q2-m7_to_lite-freshfix-20260407-175900`, using GPUs `0/1/2` and a single self-consistent artifact chain from `capture_pair` through `strict_eval`. The strict runtime bug that previously crashed semantic residual-blend patch layers without base KV entries was fixed before this rerun. All six stages succeeded, and the resulting route was `reuse=[0,1,2,3,4,5,9]`, `patch=[12,20,28,29,30,31]`, `fallback=[6,7,8,10,11,13,14,15,16,17,18,19,21,22,23,24,25,26,27]`, `recompute=[]`. However, the fresh strict metrics remain weak on this direction: `full_consumer` reached `F1 0.0630 / TTFT 47.84 ms`, while `reuse_only`, `reuse_fallback`, `reuse_patch`, and `reuse_patch_recompute` reached `F1 0.0102 / 0.0472 / 0.0253 / 0.0302` with TTFT `45.02 / 64.48 / 68.34 / 74.99 ms`, respectively, so this rerun supplies a clean rebuttal-ready artifact chain but does not support a strong transfer-quality claim on this pair.
experiment.streaming_patch_runtime_summary: On April 2, 2026, the Qwen3-1.7B self-self all-layer identity patch route was pushed through four runtime steps on A800: monolithic loading, true sharded streaming, sharded plus persistent shard and rotary caching, and finally sharded plus cache plus prewarm. The patch checkpoint was reduced from about 45G to about 449M on disk, and strict no-fallback reuse_patch preserved F1 0.7376 throughout while TTFT fell from 174703.75 ms to 18324.25 ms to 2002.10 ms and finally to 46.22 ms. In the final serving-style run, patch_shard_load_ms and patch_shard_gpu_copy_ms were fully removed from the timed path, patch_infer_ms fell to 19.44 ms, and reuse_patch finished only about 4.75 ms slower than same-run full_consumer at 41.47 ms, so the catastrophic runtime bottleneck is now resolved for the self-self identity setting.
experiment.qwen17_self_true_patch_only_summary: A dedicated `patch_only` runtime branch was added on April 2, 2026 and validated on `ser` for the Qwen3-1.7B self-self all-28 patch route. This branch skips the old reuse scaffold entirely and requires full layer coverage by patch layers. On 50 CMRC samples, the new `patch_only` method preserved the same quality as the earlier healthy all-28 `reuse_patch` route, reaching F1 0.7700 and EM 0.46, while TTFT fell from 167.74 ms to 61.04 ms and payload fell from 82.63 MB to 41.32 MB. This confirms that for a full-layer patch route with no fallback and no recompute, the reuse scaffold was redundant runtime overhead rather than an effective part of the algorithm.
experiment.qwen17_self_aligned_baseline_reuse_patch: A same-run aligned comparison was completed on April 2, 2026 on `ser` for Qwen3-1.7B self-self over 50 CMRC samples with `baseline`, `reuse_only`, and strict `patch_only` under no fallback and no recompute. With the cache-boundary-aligned `decode_first` definition enabled for the baseline, aligned baseline reached F1 0.7462 and TTFT 62.38 ms, reuse_only reached F1 0.7372 and TTFT 32.38 ms, and patch_only reached F1 0.7700 and TTFT 56.25 ms. Patch-only therefore improved both quality and TTFT versus the aligned baseline, while reuse-only remained the fastest route but with lower quality than both baseline and patch-only.
experiment.qwen17_self_alllayers_identity_patchonly: On April 3, 2026, a synthetic all-layer identity-residual `patch_only` route was run on `ser` for Qwen3-1.7B self-self over 50 CMRC samples. The checkpoint was rebuilt from the healthy mixed all-28 patch checkpoint into a sharded `patch_ckpt_sharded_v1` bundle with `residual_layers=[0..27]`, all-layer identity hints, `layers_per_shard=4`, and dropped identity residual state, reducing the timed shard bundle to about 448 MB. With two runtime fixes on `ser`—skipping prewarm module loads for identity-hinted layers and avoiding eager `direct_wk/direct_wv` reads on residual layers—the route ran successfully and reached F1 0.7462, EM 0.38, and TTFT 48.20 ms, with patch_infer 23.81 ms, patch_kproj_vproj 3.82 ms, patch_knorm 4.14 ms, patch_rotary 6.18 ms, and zero timed shard load/copy cost.
experiment.qwen17_self_alllayers_residual_approx_su: On April 3, 2026, a practical non-identity all-layer residual approximation was tested on `ser` for Qwen3-1.7B self-self by training `xnorm_nativekv_residual_mlp_v1` on all 28 layers with a smaller residual MLP (`hidden=2048`, `2` blocks) over a 12-chunk subset for 2 epochs, then reshaping the result into a 7-shard runtime bundle. The trained checkpoint reached about 6.56 GB on disk and the strict `patch_only` run reached F1 0.7462, EM 0.38, and TTFT 70.52 ms with patch_infer 38.98 ms. Training metrics show why this did not become meaningfully non-identity: under self-self supervision, the initialization already satisfies `xb_target = xa`, so the best residual solution stayed at zero-delta identity on every checked layer, while the larger materialized checkpoint only increased runtime overhead relative to the compact synthetic identity-hinted route.
experiment.implementation_scaffold_summary: Task 4 is now in progress with a project-local implementation scaffold. The workspace contains a config-driven pair-screening CLI, a config-driven original-SCD aggregation CLI, patch-layer selection using restore-one plus greedy gains, a model-inventory layer, a pair-metric builder, a trace-capture planner, a runtime environment checker, and a baseline-config builder. The chain has been validated on smoke inputs from inventory to claim-gap outputs. The scaffold remains intentionally honest: it does not fabricate real checkpoints or traces, and the current workspace runtime is not yet ready for real Qwen trace capture because torch, transformers, datasets, accelerate, safetensors, and sentencepiece are missing.
experiment.runtime_env_summary: The current workspace can compile and run the config/build/planning code, but it cannot yet execute real Hugging Face Qwen trace capture. A direct runtime check found that torch, transformers, datasets, accelerate, safetensors, and sentencepiece are all missing from the active Python environment.
experiment.trace_plan_summary: The workspace now emits an explicit producer/consumer trace plan for a selected pair, including prompt manifest path, layer list, tensor list, and per-role output directories under Experiment/datasets/traces. This plan is a scheduling/interface artifact only and does not imply traces have been collected.
experiment.remote_asset_audit_summary: Remote host ser is now confirmed as the practical execution environment for real runs. The remote reproduction repo still explains the earlier Qwen3-1.7B near-pair results, which already suggest that higher pair similarity alone does not automatically recover the paper-style TTFT-quality claim. For the stricter Qwen3.5 branch, the missing producer checkpoint blocker is now closed: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base was downloaded to /disk_n/c101-3-1/models/Qwen3.5-4B-Base and both producer and consumer load through AutoModelForCausalLM as Qwen3_5ForCausalLM. The new blocker is more fundamental: real smoke capture shows that Qwen3.5 uses hybrid cache/state semantics that the current KV-only SCD reproduction pipeline does not faithfully support.
experiment.qwen17_clean_rerun_summary: A cleaner rerun of Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 completed on March 29, 2026 and materially improved the stored reuse_fallback and reuse_patch numbers, but it still did not recover the paper-style TTFT-quality sweet spot. Full consumer remained the best high-quality operating point at 58.81 ms TTFT and F1 0.6945; reuse_fallback retained about 95.1% of full-consumer F1 but was still 1.21x slower in TTFT, while reuse_patch retained about 72.1% of full-consumer F1 and was 1.29x slower.
experiment.qwen17_routeb_directkv_summary: Route B (State -> direct KV) completed on March 30, 2026 for the runnable near-pair Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. The direct-KV patch run produced F1 0.4951 and TTFT 54.22 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 45.42 ms in the same run. Normalized against full consumer, Route B retained about 71.3% of F1 at 1.194x TTFT. This improved the normalized latency ratio relative to the clean original semantic-patch rerun (1.290x -> 1.194x) but did not rescue the claim because quality was slightly worse than the clean semantic patch and much worse than reuse_fallback, while TTFT still remained slower than native full-consumer.
experiment.qwen35_true_pair_asset_plan_summary: The strict-Qwen3.5 branch remains centered on Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base -> local Qwen3.5-4B because the local post-trained model card identifies Qwen3.5-4B-Base as its base model, making this the cleanest same-size same-family pair for the ICML story. That asset branch is now materially in place on ser. The main execution blocker has changed from checkpoint acquisition to faithful state capture: Qwen3.5 is a hybrid linear/full-attention architecture, so the current original-SCD repo cannot yet interpret its runtime cache as standard per-layer KV tuples across the full stack.
experiment.qwen35_modelscope_download_handoff_summa: The primary producer checkpoint Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base has now been successfully downloaded on ser to /disk_n/c101-3-1/models/Qwen3.5-4B-Base. The helper scripts remain useful as documentation, but the actual successful path was an inline remote ModelScope command rather than the prepared wrapper, which currently mixes local and remote paths.
experiment.qwen35_hybrid_cache_blocker_summary: A real smoke run on ser exposed a more fundamental blocker for faithful original-SCD evaluation on the strict Qwen3.5 pair. Qwen3.5-4B-Base and Qwen3.5-4B use a hybrid text architecture with linear_attention on 24 of 32 layers and full_attention on only 8 layers, and transformers 5.3.0 returns a Qwen3_5DynamicCache containing attention key/value caches plus convolution and recurrent states. The current SCD reproduction repo assumes iterable per-layer KV tuples across all layers, so pair capture fails before training. This means the strict Qwen3.5 branch is now blocked by cache-semantics mismatch rather than missing checkpoints.
experiment.qwen17_routea_state_native_summary: Pure Route A (State -> State -> native Wk/Wv -> KV) completed on March 30, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. The route-A reuse_patch path collapsed to F1 0.0000 and EM 0.000 at TTFT 54.55 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 39.94 ms in the same run. Normalized against full consumer, Route A retained 0.0% of F1 at 1.366x TTFT, making it clearly worse than both the clean original semantic patch rerun and Route B direct-KV. This establishes pure Route A as a negative result on the runnable near-pair rather than a rescue of the paper claim.
experiment.qwen17_routec_state_recompute_summary: Route C (State -> State -> suffix recompute on B) completed on March 30, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. Using the Route A state-only patch checkpoint plus a one-layer default short recompute in strict runtime, the reuse_patch_recompute path reached F1 0.6195 and EM 0.315 at TTFT 64.71 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 37.09 ms in the same run. This corresponds to 89.2% F1 retention at 1.745x TTFT versus full consumer. Route C therefore repaired the catastrophic Route A collapse, but it still failed the paper claim and was dominated by same-run reuse_fallback, which achieved higher F1 (0.6605) at lower TTFT (54.10 ms).
experiment.qwen17_routec_aligned_ttft_summary: A matched first-token timing rerun completed on March 30, 2026 for the Qwen3-1.7B to Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 Route C setup. After forcing full_consumer to use the same cache-based first-token measurement as transfer methods, full_consumer.decode_first_ms rose from about 0.09 ms to 24.42 ms, which matches the 23.2 to 23.4 ms range of the transfer paths. Under this aligned definition, full_consumer reached F1 0.6904 at TTFT 69.33 ms, while reuse_patch_recompute reached F1 0.6195 at TTFT 69.83 ms and reuse_fallback remained the strongest practical path at F1 0.6605 and TTFT 60.99 ms. The first-token discrepancy is therefore a measurement-boundary artifact, while the remaining Route C latency cost is still dominated by patch inference plus recompute rather than decode-first.
experiment.qwen17_aligned_ttft_total_summary: Matched first-token timing reruns completed on March 30, 2026 for the clean original semantic patch run and the Route B direct-KV run, complementing the earlier Route C aligned rerun. Across all three runs, full_consumer.decode_first_ms rises from the old near-zero values to about 24.4 to 27.6 ms when measured with the same cache-based first-token path as transfer methods, which matches the 23.2 to 23.8 ms range of the reuse paths. This confirms that the earlier full_consumer decode-first advantage was a measurement-boundary artifact. Under the aligned definition, clean original reuse_patch runs at 65.52 ms TTFT with F1 0.5010, Route B reuse_patch runs at 55.61 ms TTFT with F1 0.4951, and Route C reuse_patch_recompute runs at 69.83 ms TTFT with F1 0.6195, while reuse_fallback remains the strongest practical path in every aligned rerun. The aligned view therefore shifts the interpretation from a decode-first anomaly to the more substantive trade-off: clean original and Route B gain TTFT but lose too much quality, whereas Route C restores quality but is still dominated by reuse_fallback.
experiment.qwen17_nofallback_routeabc_summary: Strict no-fallback reruns completed on March 31, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. Route A reuse_patch reached F1 0.0000 at 33.76 ms TTFT versus same-run full_consumer 73.14 ms; Route B reuse_patch reached F1 0.0000 at 35.69 ms versus full_consumer 86.99 ms; Route C reuse_patch_recompute reached F1 0.0000 at 46.05 ms versus full_consumer 66.76 ms. These reruns establish that none of the three routes recovers the paper claim under the user's no-fallback definition.
experiment.qwen17_routea_state_native_nofallback_su: Strict no-fallback Route A completed on March 31, 2026. The reuse_patch path reached F1 0.0000 and EM 0.000 at 33.76 ms TTFT, versus same-run full_consumer F1 0.6904 and TTFT 73.14 ms.
experiment.qwen17_routeb_directkv_nofallback_summar: Strict no-fallback Route B completed on March 31, 2026. The reuse_patch path reached F1 0.0000 and EM 0.000 at 35.69 ms TTFT, versus same-run full_consumer F1 0.6904 and TTFT 86.99 ms.
experiment.qwen17_routec_state_recompute_nofallback: Strict no-fallback Route C completed on March 31, 2026. The reuse_patch_recompute path reached F1 0.0000 and EM 0.000 at 46.05 ms TTFT, versus same-run full_consumer F1 0.6904 and TTFT 66.76 ms.
experiment.qwen17_to_bf16_shared_patchonly_all28_su: Option 3 was completed on April 3, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 under the user's strict no-fallback definition. This route kept all 28 patch layers active but replaced the previous per-layer residual stack with a shared all-layer xnorm-nativekv residual parameterization plus a batched runtime path for consumer-native projection, k_norm, and rotary. On 50 CMRC samples, baseline reached F1 0.7408 and TTFT 103.26 ms, reuse_only remained broken at F1 0.0055 and TTFT 152.41 ms, and patch_only shared reached F1 0.7457 and EM 0.38 at TTFT 112.05 ms. Relative to the previous all-layer per-layer-MLP patch_only run on the same pair, quality stayed unchanged while TTFT fell from 176.10 ms to 112.05 ms and patch_infer_ms fell from 147.61 ms to 86.06 ms. The shared trainer's best checkpoint stayed at identity initialization, so this route functions as a runtime optimization rather than a better learned hidden-state transport map.
experiment.qwen17_self_allreuse_diagnosis_summary: The self-self reuse diagnosis now has a strict reset interpretation. Fresh reruns first showed that grouped shared-z reuse remains broken even on Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B, while layerwise group_size=1 reuse is nearly lossless. A batched fast path then reduced layerwise reuse_only TTFT from 65.48 ms to 40.67 ms by removing the serial encode bottleneck, and later timing cleanups switched transfer_ms to actual measured transport while separating rebuild from transport copy. Under the canonical no-fallback actual-transfer run, full_consumer reached F1 0.7462 and TTFT 85.82 ms, versus reuse_only F1 0.7372 and TTFT 39.78 ms with encode_ms 0.42, transfer_ms 6.46, rebuild_ms 7.17, and decode_first_ms 25.74. This repaired layerwise route is now the only valid reuse baseline; grouped/shared-z reuse remains archived failure evidence only.
experiment.qwen17_self_patch_route_diagnosis_summar: Follow-up strict self-self patch repair on March 31, 2026 showed that the earlier direct-KV collapse on Qwen3-1.7B came from two implementation bugs rather than from the patch idea alone: pair capture was silently truncating training prefixes to 256 tokens, and the Qwen direct-KV path used a target/runtime formulation that did not match Qwen attention's k_proj -> k_norm -> native rotary semantics. After fixing max-length precedence, introducing direct_kv_knorm_v1, and switching runtime to consumer-native rotary, the strict no-fallback all-28-layer patch route still failed at F1 0.0119 and TTFT 75.35 ms, but the layer-0-excluded route with patch layers 1..27 reached F1 0.7425, EM 0.44, and TTFT 88.10 ms on 50 CMRC samples. A dedicated layer-0 control audit then resolved the remaining ambiguity: xnorm_a.0 and xnorm_b.0 are exactly identical in self-self mode, consumer-native k_proj/v_proj plus k_norm and native rotary reconstruct the true layer-0 KV almost exactly, and oracle_kv_patchonly on layer 0 matches reuse_only, while the learned layer-0 translator still collapses. A direct nonlinear follow-up using the repo's existing xnorm_semantic_v1 PatchMLP route also failed completely: the all-28-layer route reached F1 0.0000 at 102.16 ms TTFT and the excl0 route also stayed at F1 0.0000 at 126.85 ms, with saved checkpoint metrics showing low hidden MSE only for layers 0..2 and sharp divergence through deeper layers. A stronger direct-KV residual MLP follow-up then kept the repaired linear route for all layers and added a 4096-wide 4-block residual model only on layer 0, but that also failed to rescue the broken layer: the all-28-layer route reached only F1 0.0087 at 193.11 ms TTFT, the dedicated layer-0-only control reached F1 0.0113 at 177.57 ms, and the excl0 route merely preserved the earlier healthy linear result at F1 0.7425 while becoming slower at 122.10 ms. A final route-2 parameterization change then fixed the quality problem: xnorm_nativekv_residual_mlp_v1 learns a hidden residual on layer 0 and lets the consumer derive KV natively, so the strict all-28-layer self-self patch run reached F1 0.7700, EM 0.46, and TTFT 200.01 ms while the layer-0-only control matched reuse_only and oracle_kv_patchonly at F1 0.7372. A runtime-only identity-skip follow-up then removed useless residual MLP inference when the selected layer-0 solution stayed at identity initialization. That preserved quality and reduced latency on the layer-0-using routes: all-28-layer TTFT fell to 167.74 ms with patch_infer_ms 97.44, and the layer-0-only control fell to 140.55 ms with patch_infer_ms 74.26. A final runtime prewarm follow-up then showed that this apparent warm-start overhead affected both layer-0-only and all-28-layer means. After preloading the runtime patch module outside timed evaluation, the strict layer-0-only reuse_patch route preserved F1 0.7372 and EM 0.38 while TTFT fell to 73.67 ms and patch_infer_ms fell to 1.42, close to oracle_kv_patchonly at 63.94 ms. The same prewarm treatment on the strict all-28-layer route preserved F1 0.7700 and EM 0.46 while TTFT fell further to 99.14 ms and patch_infer_ms to 33.26. This shows the old layer-0 collapse was a direct-KV parameterization failure rather than a runtime overwrite bug, and the remaining speed question is now the steady-state all-28-layer patch path rather than warm-start artifacts.
experiment.current_progress_summary: A consolidated status memo now has an April 4, 2026 route lock on top of the earlier April 3 reset. The main points are: faithful Qwen3.5 baseline remains blocked by hybrid cache semantics rather than missing checkpoints; on runnable Qwen3-1.7B near-pair runs, strict no-fallback Route A/B/C all fail; and both the reuse and patch stories have now been cleaned up enough to lock the default methods. The only valid reuse route is the repaired clean layerwise path with group_size=1, batched encode/decode, actual-transfer timing, pure rebuild accounting, no fallback, and no recompute. The only valid patch route is the current strict patch-only branch with no reuse scaffold, no fallback, no recompute, shared native-KV residual patching, K-only rotary, fused batched `k_proj/v_proj`, and fused K-only `k_norm`. Old grouped/shared-z reuse runs, old TTFT totals with mixed transport accounting, fallback-dependent reuse comparisons, `reuse_patch`, `reuse_patch_recompute`, and older patch fit families are now deprecated for claim judgment and retained only as debugging history. On the current default non-self reference pair Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-gray, the final optimized same-run comparison reaches baseline F1 0.7358 and TTFT 99.05 ms, repaired reuse-only F1 0.7775 and TTFT 58.11 ms, and patch-only F1 0.7547 and TTFT 63.96 ms. So the repaired clean reuse route remains the overall winner, while the locked patch-only route is now latency-competitive and faster than baseline.
experiment.qwen17_to_gray_progress_summary: The new close-pair rerun for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-gray is now complete under the cleaned protocol. A corrected 200-sample CMRC capture was rebuilt, the repaired layerwise reuse checkpoint trained successfully, and layer profiling confirmed that this pair is materially harder than the bf16 pair, with deep-layer reuse and patch errors rising sharply. After fixing subset packaging and forcing the explicit all-layer route, shared all-28 patch training, resharing, and strict evaluation all completed on ser. A later runtime optimization pass then targeted the patch bottleneck directly: key-only rotary removed useless work on `V`, `k_proj/v_proj` was fused into one batched projection, and `k_norm` was fused into that path on the `K` half only. The final optimized same-run comparison on 50 CMRC samples reached baseline F1 0.7358 and TTFT 99.05 ms, repaired reuse-only F1 0.7775 and TTFT 58.11 ms, and shared patch-only F1 0.7547 and TTFT 63.96 ms. The original gray-pair patch bottleneck was therefore real and mostly runtime-side rather than bandwidth-side: patch compute fell sharply, and the remaining patch-side variance is now dominated by fused native projection plus some shard load/copy jitter rather than standalone `k_norm` or rotary.
experiment.qwen17_to_gray_result_summary: On the cleaned Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-gray no-fallback branch, the first strict shared patch-only run exposed a real runtime bottleneck: baseline reached F1 0.7358 and TTFT 140.18 ms, repaired reuse-only reached F1 0.7775 and TTFT 45.48 ms, and shared patch-only reached F1 0.7667 but TTFT 159.47 ms because patch_infer stayed at 132.93 ms, dominated by separate native projection, `k_norm`, and rotary stages. A follow-up runtime-only optimization then fixed that path by using key-only rotary, fused `k_proj/v_proj`, and fused K-only `k_norm`. In the final optimized same-run comparison, baseline reached F1 0.7358 and TTFT 99.05 ms, repaired reuse-only reached F1 0.7775 and TTFT 58.11 ms, and shared patch-only reached F1 0.7547 and TTFT 63.96 ms with patch_infer 36.29 ms, patch_kproj_vproj 26.26 ms, patch_knorm 0.00 ms, and patch_rotary 1.63 ms. This pair therefore still favors the repaired reuse route overall, but the shared patch-only route is now latency-competitive and no longer misses the TTFT target because of standalone `k_norm` or rotary overhead.
experiment.qwen17_to_gray_patch_runtime_opt_summary: A dedicated runtime optimization follow-up was completed on April 3, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-gray strict patch-only serving. The final path removed useless work on `V` and fused the remaining `K` path: native rotary is now applied to `K` only, `k_proj/v_proj` are fused into a single batched projection, and `k_norm` is fused into that same path on the `K` half only. Across the four-step trace, patch-only TTFT fell from 159.47 ms to 119.63 ms to 68.64 ms and finally to 63.96 ms, while patch_infer fell from 132.93 ms to 90.20 ms to 39.76 ms and finally to 36.29 ms. The patch compute core (`kproj/vproj + knorm + rotary`) dropped from 128.45 ms to 27.89 ms, and standalone `patch_knorm_ms` was fully removed from the timed path. In the final same-run comparison, baseline reached F1 0.7358 and TTFT 99.05 ms, reuse-only reached F1 0.7775 and TTFT 58.11 ms, and patch-only reached F1 0.7547 and TTFT 63.96 ms. The remaining patch bottleneck is now fused native projection plus shard residency variance, not `V` normalization or standalone `k_norm`.
experiment.mistral_cross_pair_locked_routes_summary: Strict no-fallback cross-model locked-route comparisons were rerun on April 5, 2026 for both MistralLite -> Mistral-7B and Mistral-7B -> MistralLite after tightening patch-only TTFT accounting to charge encode, transfer, wall-clock patch compute, and decode-first explicitly. Reuse-only remained unusable in both directions despite large nominal speedups: it reached only F1 0.0117 at 33.39 ms and F1 0.0212 at 33.60 ms against baselines 0.6185 at 127.86 ms and 0.7829 at 122.50 ms. Patch-only remained the only healthy cross-model route, but the latency story became direction-dependent. On MistralLite -> Mistral-7B, patch-only reached F1 0.8072 at 121.48 ms, so quality improved strongly but TTFT was only about 1.05x faster than baseline because patch_shard_load dominated patch compute. On Mistral-7B -> MistralLite, patch-only reached F1 0.7528 at 75.94 ms, retaining about 96.1% of baseline F1 at about 1.61x TTFT speedup. The Mistral-family cross-pair conclusion is therefore narrower than before: reuse-only is still broken, patch-only is still the only viable transfer route, but its strict TTFT advantage is modest in one direction and substantial only in the other.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_fulldev_locked_r: A full-dev strict no-fallback rerun completed on April 5, 2026 for MistralLite -> Mistral-7B over the full CMRC2018 dev split with 3219 QA pairs, using the locked three-method comparison and isolated-process patch-only merging. Baseline reached F1 0.6911, EM 0.4427, and TTFT 133.39 ms. Reuse-only remained broken at F1 0.0109, EM 0.0000, and TTFT 38.49 ms despite the large speedup. Patch-only remained healthy at full-dev scale and became the clear winner on this direction, reaching F1 0.7898, EM 0.5769, and TTFT 67.37 ms. So on the current full-dev MistralLite -> Mistral-7B reference, patch-only improves both quality and TTFT relative to baseline, while reuse-only remains unusable.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_patchonly_train5: A train-split online check completed on April 5, 2026 for the frozen MistralLite -> Mistral-7B strict patch-only route. To force the evaluator onto CMRC2018 train, a temporary train-only data root was used so the loader fell through from missing dev to cmrc2018_train.json. On the first 50 train QA pairs, patch-only reached F1 0.6676, EM 0.2800, and TTFT 76.44 ms, with encode 0.98 ms, transfer 9.68 ms, patch_infer 39.45 ms, and decode_first 26.34 ms. This gives a direct online-phase train-split reference for the current canonical patch-only branch on the active Mistral cross-pair.
experiment.qwen17_self_patch_xnorm_nativekv_residua: An April 1, 2026 probe tested whether the C-style hidden-residual patch route could be extended from layer 0 to all 28 patch layers in the clean self-self setting. To isolate runtime feasibility rather than training quality, the run used a synthetic checkpoint whose residual modules were identity-initialized on every layer. The result failed before the first evaluated sample: the synthetic all-layer checkpoint expanded from about 2.15 GB to about 47.45 GB on disk, and strict no-fallback evaluation on a 24 GB 4090D consumer GPU OOMed while loading the patch bundle, with the process already holding about 23.42 GiB on the consumer. This shows that under the current checkpoint format and load path, all-layer xnorm_nativekv_residual_mlp_v1 is not currently deployment-feasible on the stable 4090D hardware, which is why the default patch split remains layer-0 residual plus deeper-layer linear direct_kv_knorm_v1.
experiment.reuse_route_reset_summary: On April 3, 2026, the reuse route was formally reset. Only the repaired clean reuse path is valid for current experiments: layerwise group_size=1 reuse with batched encode/decode, actual measured transfer_ms, pure rebuild_ms accounting, and no fallback by default. All older grouped/shared-z reuse results, old TTFT totals that mixed modeled transfer with staging copy, and any fallback-dependent reuse comparisons are now archived only as debugging evidence and must not be used for claims, tables, or model-pair selection.
experiment.transfer_route_lock_summary: On April 5, 2026, the current default transfer methods were re-locked with the final serving semantics now fixed. Going forward, only three methods are valid for default experiments, tables, and claim-facing comparisons: baseline, repaired reuse-only, and current strict patch-only. Repaired reuse-only is fixed to the clean layerwise route with group_size=1, batched encode/decode, actual measured transfer timing, pure rebuild accounting, no fallback, no recompute, and TTFT charged as encode plus transfer plus rebuild plus decode-first. Current strict patch-only is fixed to the dedicated patch-only runtime branch with no reuse scaffold, no fallback, no recompute, fit family `xnorm_nativekv_shared_residual_mlp_v1`, hidden transport `xnorm_a -> xb_hat`, consumer-native `Wk/Wv`, and only the consumer architecture's required post-projection operators. Patch-only TTFT is charged strictly as encode plus transfer plus wall-clock patch_infer plus decode-first, and Mistral-family patch-only must be benchmarked in an isolated fresh process when shared-process evaluation perturbs patch projection time. Older grouped/shared-z reuse, `reuse_fallback`, `reuse_patch`, `reuse_patch_recompute`, and older patch fit families are now archived-only and must not be used in the default story.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_single_layer_rep: On April 6, 2026, a replay-top3 check was run for the MistralLite -> Mistral-7B single-layer hybrid search by reusing the existing b1 first-pass results and strictly replaying the top-3 candidate layers only. Replay showed that the old single-pass winner layer 4 was unstable, and that the old TTFT-first ranking would instead pick layer 18 after replay, yielding F1 0.5836 / EM 0.250 / TTFT 61.71 ms, which is faster but clearly worse in quality than patch-only. Replay also exposed a better operating point at layer 10: F1 0.6482 / EM 0.305 / TTFT 66.05 ms, which improves both quality and TTFT over patch-only (0.6285 / 0.285 / 68.79 ms). The searcher has now been updated so replay-stage selection defaults to quality_threshold_ttft_first with relative F1 drop <= 5% versus patch-only and EM ignored by default; under this verified replay set, the default single-layer hybrid choice remains reuse layer 10.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_single_layer_loc: The current lightweight selector-locked single-layer hybrid route for MistralLite -> Mistral-7B is now frozen as reuse layer 10, chosen from replay-top3 under the rule relative F1 drop <= 5% versus patch-only with EM ignored and TTFT used only inside the quality-passing set. This locked route reaches F1 0.6482 / EM 0.305 / TTFT 66.05 ms versus patch-only at 0.6285 / 0.285 / 68.79 ms.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_singlelayer_true: A true full-rerun single-layer search on ser superseded the earlier lightweight selector lock. The full rerun completed the entire step-1 single-layer scan and replay-top3 under the new replay rule, and after correcting an execution bug that had allowed the search to continue into multi-layer greedy step 2, the valid single-layer winner was frozen and strictly finalized. The true full-rerun first-pass top-3 were layers 12, 14, and 4; replay-top3 were 14, 12, and 4; all three replayed candidates passed the relative F1 drop <= 5% gate versus patch-only; and the selector therefore chose layer 14 by quality_threshold_ttft_first. Final strict numbers are baseline F1 0.5969 / EM 0.250 / TTFT 103.78 ms, reuse-only 0.0141 / 0.000 / 33.41 ms, patch-only 0.6285 / 0.285 / 54.01 ms, and hybrid with reuse layer 14 at 0.6216 / 0.300 / 51.60 ms. This is a real latency-quality trade-off point, but not a Pareto win over patch-only: TTFT improves by 2.41 ms, F1 drops by 0.00698, and EM improves by 0.015.
experiment.mistrallite_to_mistral7_multilayer_stric: On April 7, 2026, the MistralLite -> Mistral-7B multi-layer greedy search was re-audited under the user's strict rule: at each replay step, keep only candidates with relative F1 drop <= 5% versus patch-only and stop immediately when no replay candidate passes. The searcher was fixed so an empty replay quality-pass set now stops with no_replay_quality_pass instead of continuing through a fallback decision path, which invalidates the earlier over-extended route. Auditing the completed ser replay artifacts showed that step 14 still had 2 quality-passing replay candidates but step 15 had 0, so the correct strict-stop final route is the route at the start of step 15: reuse layers [2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30] and patch layers [0, 1, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 28, 29, 31], with fallback=[] and recompute=[]. Fresh strict finalization measured baseline F1 0.5969 / EM 0.250 / TTFT 103.62 ms, reuse-only 0.0141 / 0.000 / 33.52 ms, patch-only 0.6285 / 0.285 / 53.93 ms, and hybrid 0.6072 / 0.250 / 46.18 ms. So under the user's actual objective, a valid 14-layer reuse route exists: relative to patch-only it saves 7.75 ms TTFT while giving up 0.0213 absolute F1, which stays inside the allowed 5% relative F1-drop budget of 0.03143.

publication.paper_outline: 1) Motivation and problem statement: does the original SCD method work on more similar models? 2) Qwen3.5 pair-screening protocol and baseline setup. 3) Original SCD evaluation on similar pairs. 4) Route A/B/C follow-up protocols. 5) Main results: baseline claim gap, route comparison, and TTFT-quality trade-offs. 6) Failure analysis, boundary conditions, and what pair similarity does or does not fix. 7) Reproducibility details, limitations, and implications for future cache transfer work.
publication.figures_tables_plan: Figures should cover the pair-screening pipeline, paper-claim versus measured-baseline comparisons, layerwise similarity heatmaps, TTFT-quality Pareto plots, original-versus-route-A/B/C comparisons, and representative failure cases. Tables should cover model-pair inventory, baseline settings, main benchmark outcomes, and budget-sensitive ablations.
publication.artifact_plan: Maintain experiment configs, pair lists, trace extraction scripts, evaluation summaries, and paper-ready plots/tables inside the project workspace. Prepare an anonymized reproducibility package before submission.
submission_checklist: Every headline claim must map to measured TTFT, KL/PPL, and task metrics from logged runs.
The submission must clearly distinguish original-SCD baseline results from follow-up route A/B/C results.
All figures and tables must trace back to versioned experiment outputs in the workspace.
The paper must document compute constraints, especially the short-burst nature of A800 access.
The anonymous artifact package must include enough configuration detail to reproduce the main validation pipeline.

decisions: 2026-04-04: ser 线程后端诊断完成。当前 Mistral 实验主路径主要由 PyTorch 驱动，底层为 OpenMP + Intel MKL；NumPy/SciPy 为 OpenBLAS，但不是当前 patch/reuse/profile 主瓶颈。
2026-04-04: 后续新启动的 Mistral self-self 远端脚本默认线程口径更新为 OMP_NUM_THREADS=32, MKL_NUM_THREADS=32, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=32；原始 MistralLite 运行保持旧启动环境并已完成。

2026-04-04: 原始 MistralLite self-self strict 50-sample 结果已回填。本地镜像显示 baseline F1 0.7829 / TTFT 116.18 ms，reuse-only F1 0.7686 / TTFT 52.65 ms，patch-only F1 0.7875 / TTFT 68.96 ms；patch-only 质量已略高于同次 baseline，但 patch_infer 仍由 kproj/vproj 主导。
2026-04-04: 已在 ser 上启动 MistralLite self-self 优化后复跑，复用旧的 pair/reuse/profile 产物，只重训 patch-only，并启用块级 consumer-native 投影缓存、patch_batch_size=256、layer_block_size=8 和 32/32/32 线程口径。

2026-04-04: MistralLite 优化后复跑已完成。baseline 从 116.18 ms 降到 114.94 ms，reuse-only 从 52.65 ms 降到 42.48 ms，patch-only 在 F1 完全不变的情况下从 68.96 ms 升到 75.99 ms。回归主要集中在 patch_infer，尤其是 patch_kproj_vproj_ms 从 35.76 ms 增至 41.70 ms，因此这两项训练侧优化没有带来 patch-only 的正向收益。
2026-04-04: patch-only 默认训练方案已锁回优化前版本：不再默认使用块级 consumer-native Wk/Wv 缓存堆叠，也不再默认使用 patch_batch_size=256 与 layer_block_size=8；这两项优化归档为失败尝试。

2026-04-04: MistralLite runtime 侧三项优化已在锁定的 strict patch-only 路线上完成稳定复跑：consumer-native projection 预打包、fused/grouped batched k_proj/v_proj、以及单槽可复用 CUDA Graph。新图策略修复了之前按 shape 累积 graph 导致的 OOM，并完整跑完 50 个样本。

2026-04-04: 这三项 runtime 优化作为一个组合并没有改善 MistralLite patch-only 的端到端 TTFT。相对健康原始运行，patch-only F1 保持 0.7875 不变，但 TTFT 从 68.96 ms 升到 87.34 ms。与此同时，patch_kproj_vproj_ms 从 35.76 ms 降到 34.12 ms，说明投影主核本身变快；净回归主要出现在后续 patch_rotary_ms，从 1.63 ms 升到 22.43 ms，表明当前 graph 路径更可能把或暴露了下游 K/V 布局材料化开销，而不是形成端到端收益。

2026-04-04: 因此 shared native-KV runtime fastpath 只保留为显式 opt-in 能力，默认 strict patch-only 路线已切回优化前方案。当前代码默认 `runtime_shared_nativekv_fastpath=false`，只有在后续专项 benchmark 中显式打开时才会启用 prepack + fused/grouped GEMM + CUDA Graph。

2026-04-04: 对 Mistral-7B 与 MistralLite 自对比运行做了样本级诊断后，当前更合理的解释是：MistralLite 的较小 headline speedup 主要由少数 runtime 尖峰拉高均值，而不是稳定的每样本减速。reuse-only 的中位 TTFT 几乎相同（31.71 vs 31.14 ms），patch-only 的中位 TTFT 也很接近（26.09 vs 26.89 ms）。异常尖峰与 prefix 长度的相关性较弱，因此现阶段不应把该差异直接解释成清晰的模型家族效应。

2026-04-05: 已完成 Mistral-7B 与 MistralLite self-self 的 3 次 repeated eval-only 复查，并把 repeat 产物镜像到本地。结论需要按路线区分：reuse-only 的较小 MistralLite headline speedup 主要是均值被少数 rebuild 尖峰拉高，median speedup 基本不变（2.76x vs 2.74x）；但 MistralLite patch-only 在三方法共进程评测里表现出明显 heavy-tail，median speedup 仍接近 Mistral-7B（2.94x vs 2.98x），但 mean p90 TTFT 更差（150.47 ms vs 35.39 ms）。

2026-04-05: 决定性复查已完成：在保留 sample 级 breakdown 的前提下重新运行 baseline+reuse-only+patch-only 三方法共进程 full-50，MistralLite patch-only 的 heavy tail 确实重新出现。新运行中 patch-only 仍保持 F1 0.7829，但 TTFT 从 isolated patch-only-only 的 39.66 ms 回升到 69.35 ms。关键差值几乎全部落在 `patch_kproj_vproj_ms`，其均值从 6.15 ms 升到 31.56 ms，而 `patch_rotary_ms` 与 `patch_shard_load_ms` 基本不变。非首样本热 qid（如 `DEV_7_QUERY_2`、`DEV_2_QUERY_2`、`DEV_11_QUERY_2`）的 `patch_infer` 也几乎全部由 `patch_kproj_vproj` 爆炸主导。因此当前最强结论是：MistralLite patch-only 的主要问题不是 patch-only 本身，而是共享进程评测环境下 consumer-native projection 阶段的状态干扰。
